title: Smart routing fallback incident breadcrumbs (Amara)
content:
Goal: capture quick breadcrumbs for the Feb 28 regional failover where EU region started returning 5xx for a model variant and fallback didn’t kick in consistently.

High-level timeline (UTC):
- 2026-02-28 02:12: first spike in 5xx from eu-west reported by Alerts (latency + error-rate).
- 2026-02-28 02:13: automated smart-router retries observed ~40% failure on initial route.
- 2026-02-28 02:15: some requests routed to fallback region (us-west) but ~60% of affected requests remained failing because fallback selection returned incompatible model variant (quantization mismatch).
- 2026-02-28 02:22: manual override to force-region=us-west applied for critical customers.
- 2026-02-28 02:45: root cause narrowed to model-variant compatibility check missing for cross-region fallback path.

What I did (commands & outputs):
1) Quick reproduction from my laptop (curl sampling):
   curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" -d '{"model":"open-rlhf-v2-eu","input":"hello"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate 2>&1 | sed -n '1,120p'
   -> result: HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
   Response body: {"error":"upstream failure: stream closed"}  (multiple request-ids: req_8f3a1b ...)

2) Check routing decisions in router service (local debug endpoint):
   http GET http://router-debug.internal/v1/route?model=open-rlhf-v2-eu
   Response sample (filtered):
   route_id: rt-197
   preferred_region: eu-west
   fallback_policy: region,fallback_variant_list
   chosen_target: eu-west/node-43
   fallback_candidates: [us-west/node-22, eu-west-standby/node-11]
   compatibility_check: SKIPPED  <-- this is the red flag

3) Inspect router logs around 02:12: (kubectl exec into router pod):
   kubectl logs -n inference router-rt-197 | sed -n '1200,1250p'
   [02:12:03] INFO route decision req=req_8f3a1b region=eu-west target=eu-west/node-43
   [02:12:03] WARN upstream: node-43 connection reset by peer
   [02:12:03] INFO evaluating fallback candidates
   [02:12:03] INFO candidate us-west/node-22 score=0.86 compatible=true
   [02:12:03] INFO candidate eu-west-standby/node-11 score=0.45 compatible=false
   [02:12:03] ERROR failed to trigger fallback: candidate selection mismatch: no compatible candidate found

   Observed: logs say us-west/node-22 was marked compatible=true but in reality requests there returned 500 with a body: "model-variant-mismatch: quantized-int8 vs float16". So compatibility detection logic produced false positive.

4) Quick health checks on worker: (ssh into us-west/node-22):
   systemctl status redwood-runner
   tail -n 200 /var/log/redwood/runner.log | grep -i quant

   runner.log snippet: 
   [02:12:02] LOAD model open-rlhf-v2 (q8_0)
   [02:12:02] WARN kernel-fallback: using q8_0 path for weights compiled for float16 -> possible inference errors
   [02:12:02] ERROR model init failed: weight-layout-incompatible

   So node-22 reported model load warnings and then failure. Router still thought compatible.

5) Router <-> inventory inconsistency check:
   # inventory query for node capabilities
   http GET http://inventory.internal/v1/nodes/node-22 | jq .capabilities
   -> ["q8_0", "float16-emulation"]  (but float16-emulation is > partial, not safe)

   I suspect the inventory capability tag 'float16-emulation' is being treated as full float16 compatibility in the router logic (boolean).

6) Correlate with metrics in Grafana:
   - rate of 5xx spiked on eu-west ingress rules at 02:12
   - router.fallback_attempts increased but fallback_success ratio low
   - model-load-errors on node-22 correlated exactly with failures

Error snippets & sample request-ids (copied from logs):
- req_8f3a1b -> route rt-197 -> attempted us-west/node-22 -> 500 body: "model-variant-mismatch: quantized-int8 vs float16"
- req_8f3a77 -> route rt-197 -> upstream conn reset -> router reported fallback but downstream failed with "weight-layout-incompatible"
- trace_id: tr_20260228_021203_az1hn

Hypotheses (brainstorm):
- H1: Inventory capability schema allows soft-features (e.g., float16-emulation) that router code treats as equivalent to hard compatibility. Need stricter gating.
- H2: There is a race where inventory updated node capabilities after the node was evicted/undergoing model swap, router cached stale capabilities for ~30s.
- H3: Fallback logic scoring uses numeric thresholds that don't account for model precision mismatch; scoring can mark candidate as acceptable on latency/cost metric alone.
- H4: A new deploy of the runner image (2026-02-27 22:00 UTC) changed the model load failure modes and now returns a success probe earlier than actual readiness, causing false positives in health-checks.

Immediate mitigations tried:
- 02:18: manual disable use of us-west nodes for this model variant via router feature flag: router.flags.disable-node-22=true -> reduced failed attempts (temporary).
- 02:22: forced routing policy override for critical tenant(s): POST /v1/admin/force-route {tenant: X, region: us-west} -> succeeded for a subset where us-west had full float16 images.
- 02:40: rolled back runner image on node-22 to previous stable tag -> node began serving successfully, fallback success ratio improved.

Notes on why fallback sometimes "didn’t kick":
- Router's candidate selection was returning candidates but then downstream returned model load errors that the router could not pre-detect because its compatibility check is based on inventory tags and a quick health probe which can pass (process up) even if model init fails at load time.
- There is a window between health-check and model readiness where router may route traffic. Need a stronger probe (e.g., model-load-ready endpoint per node + model_id & variant checksum check).

Outstanding questions / next steps (quick list):
- Add per-node per-model readiness endpoint and wire into router compatibility_check (API proposal in linked_confluence runbook).
- Change inventory capability semantics: split capabilities into HARD_SUPPORT vs SOFT_SUPPORT. Router should only accept HARD_SUPPORT for fallbacks by default.
- Short-term: add a temporary router rule to prefer region fallback list ordering (prefer nodes with proven model-load success within last 5m).
- Add a metric: router.compatibility_false_positive_count and an alert when > 10 in 5m for any route.
- Investigate whether the recent runner change (2026-02-27 22:00) introduced the premature success probe behavior. Roll forward an agent fix to health probe if confirmed.

Notes to self / ad-hoc checklist (for handover):
- [ ] Dump router cache at 03:00 and verify TTL settings (possible race).
- [ ] Add log tag to fallback decisions to include inventory_version, model_checksum, and node-last-successful-load timestamp.
- [ ] Capture a full packet trace for one failed request (req_8f3a1b) and store under /tmp/incidents/2026-02-28/req_8f3a1b.pcap
- [ ] Prep a short postmortem draft for CS and product explaining fallback gap and customer impact (start with impact numbers from Grafana).

Other misc notes:
- Saw a Slack thread where SRE said they had applied kube-probe changes but not model readiness probes (slack link above). Pinged @olivia to confirm whether the change was rolled to all regions.
- Related PR: github.com/redwood-inference/realtime-routing/pull/213 touches compatibility logic (review comments noted by Marcus).

If I come back later: rough TL;DR to surface in postmortem:
- Symptom: EU region spike in 5xx due to model-load failures on fallback candidates.
- Root cause: router compatibility check allowed soft capability tag; health probe insufficient to detect model load failure.
- Immediate fix: prefer proven nodes, rollback runner on impacted nodes, add temporary router rule.
- Long term: enforce HARD vs SOFT capability semantics and add per-node model readiness endpoint + metric/alerting.

-- Amara

(Notes intentionally choppy — personal scratchpad. Will clean for postmortem writeup.)
